messages:
Sam Carter: Quick postmortem follow-up 10 - need final decisions on external comms: canonical statuspage labels, RCA access tiers, and how recurring flaps trigger customer notifications. I added a slim tracker: https://ourdocs.internal/incidents/INC-2026-431/tracker :clipboard:

incident-bot: Postmortem uploaded: https://ourdocs.internal/incidents/INC-2026-431/postmortem (owner: @Sam Carter) :page_facing_up:

Renee Park: Proposal: keep public taxonomy minimal: 'Operational', 'Degraded performance', 'Partial outage'. Use numeric thresholds in template rather than fuzzy language. Example: Partial outage if user errors >=1% for >5m or availability <99% for region.

Diego Morales: +1. For customer-facing RCA access, two tiers: 1) Redacted public summary posted to statuspage within a deadline (default 72h, 48h if single-team fixable). 2) Full technical RCA available to contracted customers on request within 10 business days (NDA or EA).

Ava Thompson: We should also capture approval flow: Security + Incident Owner + Legal must sign off redactions before publish. For low-risk internal logs we can let Security approve with a documented "exception_reason" in the tracker.

Sam Carter: Okay. Can we also standardize the SLA fields in the template so it auto-selects 48h vs 72h based on a "multi_team" boolean? I can update the template but need the boolean definition.

Renee Park: Define "multi_team" = incident requiring >1 distinct team to mitigate or restore (e.g., infra + runtime + network). If true -> 72h; else -> 48h. Add to template: "severity_label", "multi_team", "public_summary_deadline".

Diego Morales: For recurring flaps, propose rule: if the same subsystem has >=3 incidents in 30d -> mark as "recurring" and auto-email impacted subscribers + open a follow-up investigation ticket. I'll own the detection job (A4). Cron example: ```0 2 * * Mon /opt/bin/incident-patterns --inc INC-2026-431 --window 30d --threshold 3 --out /tmp/inc431.json```

Ava Thompson: I'll draft the redaction checklist and a sample webhook so approvers can sign off from the tracker. Minimal webhook payload example:
```json
{"incident":"INC-2026-431","action":"redaction_signoff","approver":"security@redwood.com","approved":true}
```

Sam Carter: Action owners recap from tracker: A1 statuspage copy + numeric thresholds 0 Renee to finalize; A2 template fields + auto-deadline logic 0 Sam to update; A3 redaction checklist + webhook 0 Ava to draft + Legal review; A4 recurring detection job 0 Diego to implement. I'll run a 24h check-in.

incident-bot: Reminder scheduled: A1 statuspage draft due 2026-08-12T09:00:00Z (owner: Renee Park).

Renee Park: I'll post two variants today: short statuspage blurb and a longer 72h customer summary. Tagging Legal in the tracker for redaction review.

Diego Morales: I'll wire the pattern job into the tracker and send the first weekly digest if we see repeats. ETA for initial job: 2026-08-11.

Ava Thompson: I'll share the redaction checklist and include examples of acceptable redactions to speed Legal. Will add an "exception_reason" column in tracker for Security-approved cases.

Sam Carter: Thanks team. Goal: consistent, auditable external comms and automated detection for recurring patterns. Follow-up sync tomorrow afternoon. :white_check_mark:
